slides.1.title: Five Great Portuguese Dishes × Wine Pairing Guide
slides.1.items.0.label: Bacalhau à Brás (cod with egg and potato)
slides.1.items.0.desc: Pairing: Vinho Verde Alvarinho or Bucelas Arinto. A crisp, high-acid white cuts through the saltiness of the cured fish, and the lemony acidity complements the flavour of the fish
slides.1.items.1.label: Roast suckling pig, Leitão da Bairrada
slides.1.items.1.desc: Pairing: Bairrada Baga red. The high acidity and tannin of Baga cut perfectly through the fat of the crackling, a classic example of regional pairing
slides.1.items.2.label: Douro-style braised beef
slides.1.items.2.desc: Pairing: Douro Touriga Nacional. The robust Touriga Nacional echoes the deep flavours of slow-braised beef, and tannin and protein balance perfectly
slides.1.items.3.label: Queijo da Serra (Serra da Estrela soft cheese)
slides.1.items.3.desc: Pairing: 20-year Tawny Port or Colheita. The oxidative nutty, honeyed character and the creaminess of the semi-liquid cheese make the perfect match of perfect matches
slides.1.items.4.label: Custard tart, Pastéis de Nata
slides.1.items.4.desc: Pairing: Moscatel de Setúbal or 10-year Tawny. The caramel and cinnamon notes of the tart and the oxidative honeyed character of the sweet wine make an elegant dessert pairing
slides.2.title: Port and Cheese: The Art of the Ultimate Pairing
slides.2.html:
Pairing Portuguese Port with cheese is one of the world's most famous food and wine combinations, with a tradition of several hundred years, especially in Britain.

🧀 Cheese Type × Port Match

Cheese type Recommended Port Reason for pairing
Stilton (English blue cheese) Vintage Port A classic British tradition; the saltiness of blue cheese contrasts with the fruity sweetness of Vintage
Queijo da Serra (Portuguese soft cheese) 20-year Tawny The oxidative nutty, honeyed character blends perfectly with creamy cheese
Manchego (hard sheep's cheese) LBV Port The medium sweetness of LBV balances the salty, crumbly nature of hard cheese
Fresh goat's cheese White Port The fresh almond note of White Port does not overpower the delicacy of fresh cheese

🌰 Golden Rules

  • Sweet with salty: the saltiness of the cheese makes the sweet wine seem more refined
  • Match texture: semi-liquid cheese with Tawny, hard cheese with Vintage
  • Match origin: Portuguese cheese × Portuguese Port, the best demonstration of "terroir unity"
slides.3.question: What is the ideal wine to pair with Bairrada roast suckling pig (Leitão)?
slides.3.explanation: Bairrada suckling pig with local Baga red is Portugal's most famous example of regional pairing. Baga's very high acidity and tannin effectively cut through the rich fat of the crackling, while its red-berry aromas complement the roast pork, a perfect example of "what grows together goes together".
